limitations: one global two-layer energy balance with a fixed feedback: no regional dynamics, no feedback that changes with the climate state, no carbon-cycle feedback (concentrations are prescribed)
forcing agents other than CO2, CH4 and N2O follow hand-entered indices scaled to rounded AR6 2019 estimates; the scenario paths approximate SSP1-2.6, SSP2-4.5 and SSP5-8.5
regional warming is a fixed pattern (land, Arctic, Southern Ocean) plus an aerosol and an overturning term, not a simulation
impacts use rounded literature relations (AR6 extreme frequencies reproduced by a shifted normal distribution, 7 %/K rain, linear sea ice)
the CO2 map spreads rounded national totals over boxes and distributes the land and ocean sinks by simple proxies; the concentration anomaly is a diffusion estimate
the space drivers (cosmic dust, cosmic rays, solar-wind energy) enter as bounds from the other runs

runs.description: the air over the sea keeps its initial heat and moisture (no fluxes from the ocean)
uniform soil moisture everywhere (no wet or dry regions)
no mountains (no blocking, no orographic rain)
no daytime heating and no nocturnal cooling over land

map.land_mask_source: global-land-mask 1.0.0 (MIT; GLOBE 1 km elevation, NOAA), sampled at the cell centres by tools/make_land_mask.py

climate.note: Two-layer energy balance (mixed layer + deep ocean); feedbacks rounded from the AR6 assessment (net 1.15 W/m2/K, ECS about 3.2 K); the ocean heat uptake (exchange 1.0 W/m2/K, which includes the efficacy of deep-ocean uptake) gives a transient climate response of about 1.8 K, the AR6 best estimate; ECS range 2.5-4 K for the uncertainty band.

co2_map.note: Rounded national totals of about 2022 (fossil CO2 and cement) and cumulative fossil emissions since 1850, entered by hand after the Global Carbon Budget; the regions are coarse boxes. The land sink follows a productivity proxy, the ocean sink Wanninkhof exchange with a zonal air-sea pCO2 difference; both are scaled to the budget.

ocean.note: Annual-mean air minus sea pCO2 (uatm) by |latitude|, rounded to the pattern of the Takahashi/Landschuetzer climatologies: the tropics outgas a little, the mid and high latitudes take up; the boxes above override it (upwelling regions, the Southern Ocean). The map is scaled to the total ocean sink.

history.note: Rounded observed concentrations (NOAA/AR6-like) and hand-entered indices of the other agents, 1.0 in 2019.

impacts.note: Amplification factors and the heat-extreme spread reproduce rounded AR6 relations (1-in-50-year heat 4.8x at 1 K, 14x at 2 K, 39x at 4 K); 1-in-10-year heavy rain 1.3x per K; sea ice 4.7 million km2 at 1.2 K, minus 2.9 per K.
